blocks.orig: The Ndutu Region is part of Ngorongoro Conservation Area. It stretches to the unfenced southern part of the Serengeti National Park. There is plenty of resident wildlife such as elephants, hyenas, giraffes and big cats to be found all year round.
blocks.html: The Ndutu Region belongs to the Ngorongoro Conservation Area and runs on into the unfenced southern section of the Serengeti National Park. Resident wildlife is abundant throughout the year, with elephants, hyenas, giraffes and big cats all living here.

blocks.orig: At the end of December, the Great Migration usually arrives in Ndutu with around 2 million animals. Wildebeests, zebras, and gazelles gather here to give birth and remain in the area until April. From December to March, thousands of calves are born each day. The grass is rich in nutrients for young animals, and its short length allows adults to spot predators from a distance. This makes Ndutu a safe place for young zebras and wildebeests to grow. Ndutu is a scenic region with high wildlife density. The calving season attracts many predators to the open plains, including lions, cheetahs, leopards, hyenas, and large numbers of wild dogs!
blocks.html: Around the end of December the Great Migration normally reaches Ndutu, bringing roughly 2 million animals with it. Wildebeest, zebras and gazelles assemble here to calve and stay in the area until April. Between December and March, thousands of calves arrive every single day. The grass is packed with nutrients for the young, and because it is short, the adults can see predators coming from far away. That is why Ndutu is a safe place for young zebras and wildebeest to grow up. It is a beautiful region with a very high density of wildlife. The calving season draws plenty of predators onto the open plains: lions, cheetahs, leopards, hyenas and large packs of wild dogs!

blocks.orig:
The best game viewing spot is around Lake Ndutu, where enormous herds congregate. It is a shallow alkaline lake that is located on the eastern border of the Serengeti National Park. In 1973, the shores of Lake Ndutu were the location of an archaeological excavation site about 140 square meters that led to the discovery of the Ndutu cranium and several remains of tools from over 500.000 years ago.
Today it serves as a water source for the animals and shares the same basin as lake Masek that is located a short distance east of it – but inside Ngorongoro conservation area.
The forests and granite Kopjes around Lake Ndutu are also home to lots of game outside of the migration months.
blocks.html:
The finest game viewing is found around Lake Ndutu, where the huge herds gather. This shallow alkaline lake lies on the eastern edge of the Serengeti National Park. In 1973, an archaeological dig of roughly 140 square metres on the lakeshore uncovered the Ndutu cranium together with a number of tool remains dating back more than 500.000 years.
These days the lake provides water for the animals and sits in the same basin as Lake Masek, a short way to the east, though that lake lies within the Ngorongoro Conservation Area.
The woodland and granite kopjes surrounding Lake Ndutu hold plenty of game outside the migration months as well.

blocks.orig: Olduvai Gorge (Maasai spelling is Oldupai, which means “the place of the wild sisal”) is one of the world’s most significant paleoanthropological sites. It is a steep-sided ravine in the Great Rift Valley, about 48 km long. Located 25 km from Lake Ndutu and Lake Masek, the gorge cuts into Pleistocene lake bed sediments up to a depth of 90 m. Remains of the earliest evidence of the existence of our human ancestors were found here that have proven invaluable in furthering understanding of early human evolution. The hundreds of fossils (bones) discovered here date back millions of years.
blocks.html: Olduvai Gorge (the Maasai spelling is Oldupai, meaning “the place of the wild sisal”) ranks among the most important paleoanthropological sites on earth. This steep-sided ravine in the Great Rift Valley is around 48 km long. It lies 25 km from Lake Ndutu and Lake Masek and cuts through Pleistocene lake-bed sediments to a depth of as much as 90 m. The earliest evidence of our human ancestors was unearthed here, and those finds have been invaluable for understanding early human evolution. The hundreds of fossils (bones) found at the site are millions of years old.

blocks.orig: You can also visit a small museum at this spot to learn about the fascinating excavations and discoveries that have taken place here.
blocks.html: There is also a small museum on site where you can learn more about the remarkable excavations and finds made here.

blocks.orig: The best months to visit Ndutu Region are from end of December, when the Great Migration herds start to arrive from the north, until April when the millions of wildebeest, zebra and gazelle start trekking northwards again. In the early months of the year – with a peak in February and March – the wildebeest herds are calving on the grassy plains.
blocks.html: The best time to visit the Ndutu Region runs from late December, when the Great Migration herds begin to arrive from the north, until April, when the millions of wildebeest, zebra and gazelle set off northwards once more. During the first months of the year, peaking in February and March, the wildebeest give birth on the grassy plains.

blocks.orig: Travel Tips from our experts about Ndutu

My name is Hamisi, and I am a guide in Ndutu for 15 years. Most of our guests are impressed to see so many animals at once! Of course, the Great Wildebeest Migration is an amazing spectacle to witness for all our guests. Watching the young being born and making their first steps is a great experience and offers plenty of opportunities for fantastic photographs.
blocks.html: I am Hamisi, and I have worked as a guide in Ndutu for 15 years. Most of our guests are amazed to see so many animals in one place! The Great Wildebeest Migration is of course a spectacular event for every visitor. Seeing the newborns arrive and take their first wobbly steps is a wonderful experience and gives you countless chances for superb photographs.

blocks.orig: The Ndutu Region is part of Ngorongoro Conservation Area and stretches to the southern  Serengeti. The great migration reaches here with its 2 million animals to give birth to their calves and thousands of animals are born daily between the end of December and the beginning of March. This also attracts many predators like lions and hyenas!
blocks.html: Ndutu is part of the Ngorongoro Conservation Area and extends into the southern Serengeti. The Great Migration, some 2 million animals strong, arrives here to calve, and between late December and early March thousands of young are born every day. This in turn draws plenty of predators such as lions and hyenas!
